prior_art.verdict_detail: We found no public tracker that maps rules on AI prescribing across countries and US states, or codes them by how much independence the AI has; more than 20 sources could not be checked (see coverage_limits). The closest, the Health & AI Policy Index, groups prescribing with other reserved clinical functions; Manatt's quarterly tracker describes the Utah pilots in prose. Other trackers cover general AI or health-AI law without a prescribing field, and Utah's own register covers one state. OECD.AI and WHO have no prescribing content.
prior_art.coverage_limits: The session's web-search budget ran out early, so several sources were checked only by guessed URL or not at all: Epstein Becker Green, Foley, Hogan Lovells, Covington, Husch Blackwell, FSMB (403), verticomply, startbusinessbystate, SSRN, Health Affairs, Brookings, R Street, Mercatus, Niskanen, Paragon, PPI, Abundance Institute, Institute for Progress, STAT, KFF, Axios, GitHub, Avalere. Rerun those before calling the verdict final.

items.name: Health & AI Policy Index (HAPI)
items.operator: Health & AI Policy Index (led by Will Moss); featured in npj Digital Medicine
items.scope: curated registry of laws, regulations and standards on AI in health care
items.geography: US states and federal, plus selected international frameworks
items.what_it_lacks: Broader than this page. Its five topic tags do not include prescribing, though its operational rules include one (H1) that bars AI from reserved clinical functions, prescribing among them, without licensed professional involvement. Doctronic, Legion Health and August AI each have their own entry with a summary, status and link to the signed agreement (Doctronic 'Active Pilot'; Legion Health and August AI 'Approved - demonstration not yet begun'). Nolla Health, signed 2026-09-22, was not yet listed when checked. No coding by autonomy rung, which is this page's narrower aim.
items.notes: Home page: 'Last updated November 4, 2026 · 408 policies tracked · Featured in npj Digital Medicine'. Describes itself as 'a curated, research-driven registry of laws, regulations, and standards shaping artificial intelligence in healthcare'. Keyword tags: five topics, none on prescribing. Rechecked 2026-11-12 in the fact-check pass.
items.operational_rule_h1: AI may not perform reserved clinical functions (diagnosis, treatment decisions, prescribing, formal clinical assessment) without licensed professional involvement.

items.name: Manatt Health: Health AI Policy Tracker
items.what_it_lacks: Quarterly narrative newsletter (latest Q3 2026, October 27), not a database or map; the full bill list is for subscribers. Describes all four Utah pilots in prose; no prescribing category, no state-by-state coding of AI prescribing, and no H.R. 238. US only.
items.notes: Closest law-firm product. Notes Idaho and Iowa bills would create licensed AI providers with tiered licensing by autonomy (Cicero model), not expected to advance. Counts 46 bills in 27 states on AI in care settings in 2026, 7 enacted in 6 states.

searched_nothing_found.finding: Nothing prescription-specific. CSP L.4001-3 (bioethics law 2021, art. 17) only requires informing patients and professionals when an algorithmic medical device trained on massive data is used, and explainability; no human-decision clause. HAS generative-AI guide (Oct 2025, updated 2026-04-15): 'Chaque usage d'un système d'IA générative doit être conscient, supervisé et raisonné'; no mention of prescription. HAS scoping note (validated 2025-04-02) plans good-practice recommendations covering 'la décision autonome, la vérification et contrôle humain des résultats des SIA'; final text not located (lead). CNOM and ANSM not reached.

Telemedicine avis (2026-01-23) says e-prescriptions are created on Recip-e, a rigorous clinical exam after anamnesis is 'indispensable' for diagnosis and treatment, and telemedicine as a substitute for a classic consultation should be avoided for acute conditions in unknown patients; no mention of AI, algorithms or questionnaires. Only AI item on the Ordre site is a news post on a UAntwerpen master's thesis (2026-03-27). AFMPS/FAGG and Recip-e rules not checked.

ÖÄK e-health compendium covers e-Rezept (private prescriptions digital, e-Medikation mandatory from 2026-01-01) but nothing on AI issuing or renewing prescriptions; only a quoted remark that AI will not replace the doctor. Ärztegesetz and BASG not checked.

2024 Medical Council guide has no AI text; s.34 prescribing and s.37.1 telemedicine ('must observe the same standards of conduct and practice as would be expected if treating the patient in-person'). PSI internet-supply registration covers non-prescription medicines only. HSE not checked (no search).

Closest: Läkemedelsverket press release 2026-03-04 announcing spring-2026 inspections of ambient-scribe manufacturers (MDR may apply); no prescribing content. https://via.tt.se/pressmeddelande/4272364/lakemedelsverket-granskar-ai-assistenter-i-sjukvarden?lang=sv

Only general Helsedirektoratet AI material (Felles KI-plan 2024-2025; assessment of a public AI health-question service on Helsenorge). Tidsskriftet kronikk 'Bruk av KI-verktøy på fastlegekontoret' (Nov 2025) returned 403.
Nothing on AI issuing/renewing prescriptions. DKMA AI use is internal/regulatory plus unnamed real-world-data prescribing-support pilots (decision support, below rung 1); see lead.

Tervisekassa: repeat prescriptions can be renewed by phone/email by the physician; no AI. ERR: state plans AI for documentation (ambulance AI note-drafting concept, Eesti.ai); 'Esimesi katsetusi tehisaruga tervishoius juba tehakse' (first AI trials in healthcare already under way) but nothing on prescriptions. Separate ERR item: proposal to let specialist nurses renew repeat prescriptions (human, not AI).

esveikata.lt e-prescription subsystem does automatic drug-interaction checks at issue (decision support, below rung 1). LSMU survey of family doctors cites lack of legal regulation as a barrier to AI. Nothing on AI issuing/renewing. Only one search possible (budget).

MCHK Code of Professional Conduct (rev. Oct 2022) has no AI, algorithm or telemedicine text; s.9.1 only requires a doctor to prescribe after proper consultation. No AI-prescribing rule found. Department of Health and Hospital Authority not checked.
MMC publications list has no telemedicine, AI or e-prescription guidance (latest ethics circular 2000). MOH telemedicine guidance and Telemedicine Act 1997 not opened.

MOHW 'AI Primary Healthcare Strategy' (2026-08-06) mentions only an AI assistant that explains prescriptions to patients; Dailypharm says HIRA AI focus is claims review. Neither supports the earlier lead of AI prescription review from 2028. No regulator source on AI prescribing opened (law.go.kr / mohw.go.kr not reached).
No Beijing final version found (draft only). No additional province with the clause confirmed; the province sweep was cut short by the search cap.
